decisions.reason: Having remained in the range beyond launch, this carpet still fits the firm's established materials and interior-accessories knowledge, so management would more likely refine or reposition it than withdraw it, though overlap in the carpet assortment leaves some rationalisation risk.

The hand-knotted wool silk carpet draws strongly on the firm's craftsmanship and premium-material competences, and its continued presence suggests management sees enough learnable market value to keep developing its positioning.

This low-pile decorative carpet is close to existing design and sourcing capabilities, so absorptive capacity supports continued adjustment rather than exit, but similarity to other carpet launches keeps withdrawal risk moderately elevated.
The corner bench builds directly on the firm's core furniture and project-interior expertise, making it a highly understandable extension that management is likely to retain and improve.

Although this low-pile carpet is well within the firm's knowledge base and therefore supportable, it remains the most exposed to later assortment pruning because several closely related carpet introductions compete for space in the portfolio.

The swivel shell chair line is tightly aligned with the firm's residential and workplace seating capabilities, and the multi-model format gives management room to learn from demand and fine-tune the range instead of dropping it.
